newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-ROSSET TOPPLES HENMAN TO WIN EC TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ROSSET TOPPLES HENMAN TO WIN EC TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Big-serving Swiss Marc Rosset overwhelmed British number one Tim Henman 6-2 7-5 6-4 to win the $1 million European Community tennis championship on Sunday.
It was the 12th career singles title for the 1992 Olympic champion and his first since June 1995.
Rosset, the world number 23 but unseeded here, was always in control and cancelled out most of Henman's break points with his big serve, which he repeatedly hit at more than 200 kph.
But he said afterwards he still was not entirely happy.
"I'm the kind of person who is never really satisfied. I'm happy that I won today but I was not very pleased with my game and especially with my backhand," Rosset said.
"My service was great, my backhand was rubbish."
Sixth-seeded Henman, the world number 19 who won his first ATP Tour title in Sydney last month, struggled with his own service and with Rosset's mixture of powerful ground strokes.
Rosset, who hit 16 aces in the final, believed Henman had made life easier than he had expected.
"He did not serve great, which gave me opportunities to break him. Obviously he didn't play his best tennis today.

"It could have been really different if he had had a better percentage of serve. And when I could play on his backhand with my forehand I was 99 percent sure of winning the point because he couldn't hurt me," Rosset said.
Henman, by contrast, was full of praise for his opponent.
"I've got to take my hat off to him," he said. "From the word go he played very well. I was a little disappointed with my performance but I was not really allowed to play so well.
"I had some opportunities in the second set but he was able to come up wit the big serves on the big points."
It was the third final and just the fourth defeat in less than two months for Henman, who had never before played Rosset.
Rosset is a traditionally slow starter but began well on Sunday, breaking Henman's serve in the third game and taking the first set with a love game after just 28 minutes.
Henman, who at one point threw his racket down in frustration, began to find his feet but at 5-5 in the second was broken again.
Rosset, 26, served out and got an early break in the third game of the third set.
Henman, the first Briton in the top 20 since Buster Mottram in 1982, broke back in the sixth but it was a short-lived recovery.
Rosset broke again immediately and went on to take the match after two hours and nine minutes of action.
He collected $162,500 for the victory and was also allowed to hold, briefly, a diamond-studded golden racket-shaped trophy on offer to anyone who wins the event three times in five years.
Last year's winner, Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia, pulled out on Tuesday before his scheduled first-round match because of shoulder problems.
